visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) The video opens with a vibrant title card featuring the Costco Wholesale logo prominently at the top. A cartoon character resembling Wreck-It Ralph is positioned on the left, looking surprised. Large, stylized pink and yellow text in Traditional Chinese announces the 'Costco Weekly Special Report' for the dates February 10th to February 16th. The background is a soft-focus image of white and red roses, suggesting a Valentine's Day theme. (2) The scene transitions rapidly through various aisles of a Costco warehouse. Each shot is a medium-close up of a specific product on a shelf. For example, stacks of Kleenex toilet paper are shown, followed by large bags of Arm & Hammer cat litter. Each product is accompanied by a large, centered text overlay detailing the item name, original price, discount amount, and final special price in bold colors. (3) The montage continues through the refrigerated and fresh food sections. Trays of Australian lamb chops are displayed in a glass case, followed by packages of North Sea shredded squid. The camera remains mostly static for each brief shot, relying on fast cuts to maintain a high-energy pace. The lighting is bright and even, typical of a large retail environment. (4) The final sequence covers a wide array of snacks, beverages, and household items. Brands like Snickers, Godiva, Starbucks, and Quaker are featured. The background consistently shows the industrial shelving and bulk packaging characteristic of a warehouse store. The video maintains its rapid editing style until the end, providing a comprehensive look at the week's deals.

audio_base.audio_narrative_log: (1) A high-energy male narrator begins speaking immediately with a bright, enthusiastic tone. He introduces the 'Costco Weekly Special Report' with clear articulation and a fast speech rate. Simultaneously, an upbeat electronic pop track with a tempo of approximately 128 BPM starts, featuring a driving four-on-the-floor kick drum and bright synthesizer melodies. (2) As the visual cuts begin, the narrator's voice becomes a rapid-fire delivery of product names and prices. His pitch is moderate but exhibits high variability to maintain listener engagement. The BGM remains at a consistent volume, sitting just below the vocal track in the mix, providing a rhythmic pulse that matches the editing pace. (3) The audio continues with this dense information flow. There are no significant pauses in the narration, creating a sense of urgency and excitement. Subtle 'whoosh' sound effects are occasionally heard during transitions between different product categories, adding a layer of professional sound design to the fast-paced edit. (4) The track concludes with the narrator's final price announcement. The BGM maintains its energy throughout, with no fade-out or change in texture, ending abruptly with the final visual frame. The overall mix is clean and studio-quality, with high signal-to-noise ratio and no audible environmental distractions from the warehouse.
